title.zh: 卷一百四十四 志6: 樂志上
title.raw: 卷一百四十四 志6: 樂志上 Volume 144: Treatises 6 Music 1

sentences.zh: 樂誌上

translations.literal: Music Treatise (Part One)
translations.idiomatic: Music Treatise (Part One)

sentences.zh: 古之王者，理定制禮，功成作樂，所以昭事天地，統和人神，歷代已來，舊章斯在。

translations.literal: The ancient kings, when they established order, instituted rituals; when their achievements were complete, they composed music — thereby to make clear their service to Heaven and Earth and to harmonize humans and spirits. Through successive dynasties down to the present, the old regulations have remained.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when kings had put the realm in order they established ritual, and when their achievements were complete they composed music — to make their service to Heaven and Earth manifest and to harmonize humanity with the spirits. Down through the ages, those ancient statutes have endured.

sentences.zh: 洎唐季之亂，鹹、鎬為墟；

translations.literal: By the time of the turmoil at the end of Tang, Xian and Hao lay in ruins;
translations.idiomatic: When the chaos of the late Tang came, the capitals of Xian and Hao were reduced to ruins;

sentences.zh: 梁運雖興，《英》、《莖》掃地。

translations.literal: Although the fortune of Liang rose, the Ying and Jing [pieces] were swept from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Liang dynasty arose, the Ying and Jing compositions were swept utterly away.

sentences.zh: 莊宗起於朔野，經始霸圖，其所存者，不過邊部鄭聲而已，先王雅樂，殆將泯絕。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong rose from the northern frontier and began his hegemonic enterprise; what he preserved was no more than the borderland Zheng music — the elegant music of former kings was nearly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong rose from the northern marches and set his hegemonic design in motion; all that survived was the borderland sound of Zheng — the refined music of former kings was all but lost.

sentences.zh: 當同光、天成之際，或有事清廟，或祈祀泰壇，雖簨虡猶施，而宮商孰辨？

translations.literal: During the Tongguang and Tiancheng periods, there were times when rites were performed at the Pure Temple or sacrifices offered at the Great Altar, but though the pennants and feather ornaments were displayed, who could distinguish gong from shang?
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongguang and Tiancheng eras, the Pure Temple was sometimes served or sacrifices offered at the Great Altar, yet though the feathered standards were set up, who could tell one pitch from another?

sentences.zh: 遂使磬襄、鼗武，入河、漢而不歸；

translations.literal: Thus masters like Qinxiang and Taowu entered the Yellow River and the Han and did not return;
translations.idiomatic: So masters such as Qinxiang and Taowu went into the Yellow River and the Han and never came back;

sentences.zh: 湯、舜韶，混陵谷而俱失。

translations.literal: The Shao of Tang and Shun were mingled with hills and valleys and lost together.
translations.idiomatic: The Sha music of Yu and Shun was confounded with hill and valley alike and lost entirely.

sentences.zh: 洎晉高祖奄登大寶，思迪前規，爰詔有司，重興二舞。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu suddenly ascended the great throne, he wished to follow the former regulations and therefore ordered the relevant offices to revive the Two Dances.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu suddenly took the throne, he sought to follow the precedents of old and ordered the responsible offices to restore the Two Dances.

sentences.zh: 旋屬烽火為亂，明法罔修，漢祚幾何，無暇制作。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the beacon fires of rebellion erupted, enlightened laws went unreformed, and the Han mandate lasted but a few years — there was no leisure for composition.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the beacon fires of war flared up, enlightened statutes went unreformed, and the Han mandate endured only briefly — there was no time to compose new works.

sentences.zh: 周顯德五年冬，將立歲仗，有司以崇牙樹羽，宿設於殿庭。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, when the year's court was to be established, the relevant offices set up the tooth-like frames and feather banners overnight in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Xiande under Zhou, as the annual court was about to be held, the responsible offices erected the tooth-shaped frames and feather standards overnight in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 世宗因親臨樂懸，試其聲奏，見鐘磬之類，有設而不擊者，訊於工師，皆不能對。

translations.literal: Shizong therefore came in person to inspect the suspended bells, tested their sound and performance, and saw that among bells, chimes, and the like some were set up but not struck; when he questioned the artisans, none could answer.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong came in person to examine the suspended instruments, tested their sound and performance, and found that among the bells and chime-stones some were set out but never struck; when he asked the craftsmen, none could explain it.

sentences.zh: 世宗惻然，乃命翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼參詳其制，又命樞密使王樸考正其聲。

translations.literal: Shizong was moved and ordered Hanlin Academician and Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Yan to examine the regulations in detail, and also ordered Censor-in-chief Wang Pu to correct the pitches.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Shizong ordered Hanlin Academician and Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Yan to investigate the regulations in detail, and also directed Censor-in-chief Wang Pu to correct the pitches.

sentences.zh: 樸乃用古累黍之法，以審其度，造成律準，其狀如琴而巨，凡設十三弦以定六律、六呂旋相為宮之義。

translations.literal: Pu then used the ancient method of stacked millet grains to determine the measurements, and fashioned pitch pipes — shaped like a zither but large, with thirteen strings in all to fix the mutual relations of the six lü and six tones as palaces [of the scale].
translations.idiomatic: Pu applied the ancient method of stacked millet grains to determine the measurements, fashioned pitch pipes shaped like an oversized zither, and strung thirteen strings in all to establish how the six lü and six tones rotate as the tonic.

sentences.zh: 世宗善之，申命百官議而行之。

translations.literal: Shizong approved this and ordered the hundred officials to deliberate and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong approved the plan and directed the hundred officials to deliberate and put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 今亦備紀於後，以誌五代雅樂沿革之由焉。

translations.literal: They are also recorded here in full, to set forth the course of change in the elegant music of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: They are also recorded here in full, to trace how the refined music of the Five Dynasties evolved.

sentences.zh: 梁開平初，太祖受禪，始建宗廟，凡四室，每室有登歌、酌獻之舞：肅祖宣元皇帝室曰《大合之舞》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping of Liang, when the Taizu received the abdication, he first established the ancestral temple — four chambers in all, each with ascending song and libation-offering dances: the chamber of Sizu, Emperor Xuan Yuan, was called the Dance of Great Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiping under Liang, when Taizu accepted the abdication, he first built the ancestral temple with four chambers in all; each chamber had its ascending song and libation dance — the chamber of Sizu, Emperor Xuan Yuan, used the Dance of Great Harmony.

sentences.zh: 敬祖光憲皇帝室曰《象功之舞》。

translations.literal: The chamber of Jingzu, Emperor Guangxian, was called the Dance of Symbolizing Merit.
translations.idiomatic: The chamber of Jingzu, Emperor Guangxian, used the Dance of Symbolizing Merit.

sentences.zh: 憲祖昭武皇帝室曰《來儀之舞》。

translations.literal: The chamber of Xianzu, Emperor Zhaowu, was called the Dance of Coming Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: The chamber of Xianzu, Emperor Zhaowu, used the Dance of Coming Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 烈祖文穆皇帝室曰《昭德之舞》。

translations.literal: The chamber of Liezu, Emperor Wenmu, was called the Dance of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The chamber of Liezu, Emperor Wenmu, used the Dance of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂章各一首。

translations.literal: One ascending-song hymn for each.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one ascending-song hymn.

sentences.zh: 二年春，梁祖將議郊禋，有司撰進樂名、舞名：樂曰《慶和之樂》。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, when Liang Taizu was about to deliberate on suburban and feng sacrifices, the relevant offices drafted and submitted music and dance names: the music was called Music of Celebrating Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, as Liang Taizu prepared to discuss suburban and feng sacrifices, the responsible offices submitted proposed music and dance names: the music was titled Music of Celebrating Harmony.

sentences.zh: 舞曰《崇德之舞》。

translations.literal: The dance was called the Dance of Honoring Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The dance was titled the Dance of Honoring Virtue.

sentences.zh: 皇帝行奏《慶順》。

translations.literal: When the emperor processed, Music of Celebrating Compliance was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor processed, they played Celebrating Compliance.

sentences.zh: 奠玉帛登歌奏《慶平》。

translations.literal: When jade and silk were set forth, the ascending song performed Music of Celebrating Peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the offering of jade and silk, the ascending song was Celebrating Peace.

sentences.zh: 迎俎奏《慶肅》。

translations.literal: When welcoming the offering stand, Music of Celebrating Solemnity was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When welcoming the offering stand, they played Celebrating Solemnity.

sentences.zh: 酌獻奏《慶熙》。

translations.literal: At the libation offering, Music of Celebrating Splendor was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the libation offering, they played Celebrating Splendor.

sentences.zh: 飲福酒奏《慶隆》。

translations.literal: When drinking the blessed wine, Music of Celebrating Grandeur was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When drinking the blessed wine, they played Celebrating Grandeur.

sentences.zh: 送文舞迎武舞奏《慶融》。

translations.literal: When sending off the civil dance and welcoming the martial dance, Music of Celebrating Blending was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When dismissing the civil dance and welcoming the martial dance, they played Celebrating Blending.

sentences.zh: 亞獻奏《慶和》。

translations.literal: At the secondary offering, Music of Celebrating Harmony was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the secondary offering, they played Celebrating Harmony.

sentences.zh: 終獻奏《慶休》。

translations.literal: At the final offering, Music of Celebrating Rest was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the final offering, they played Celebrating Rest.

sentences.zh: 樂章各一首。

translations.literal: One hymn for each.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one hymn.

sentences.zh: 太廟迎神，舞名《開平》。

translations.literal: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple for welcoming the spirit, the dance was called Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the dance for welcoming the spirit was titled Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 皇帝行、盥手、登歌、飲福酒、徹豆、送神，皆奏樂。

translations.literal: When the emperor processed, washed hands, ascending song, drinking blessed wine, removing the beans, and sending off the spirit — music was performed for all.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor's procession, hand-washing, ascending song, drinking the blessed wine, removal of the beans, and sending off the spirit — music was played at each.

translations.idiomatic: For the libation at the temple chamber of Tang Zhuangzong, Emperor Guang Sheng Shen Min Xiao, they performed the Dance of Martial Accomplishment.

translations.idiomatic: For the libation at the temple chamber of Han Wenzu, Emperor Mingyuan, they performed the Dance of Spiritual Endurance.

translations.literal: The texts of most hymns are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the hymn texts are not recorded here.

translations.literal: The hymns listed above
translations.idiomatic: The hymns listed above

sentences.zh: 晉天福四年十二月，禮官奏：「來歲正旦，王公上壽，皇帝舉酒，請奏《元同之樂》；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, the ritual officials memorialized: "At next year's New Year's Day, when the princes and dukes offer longevity wishes and the emperor raises his cup, please perform Music of Primal Unity;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tianfu under Jin, the ritual officials reported: "At next year's New Year's Day, when the princes and dukes offer birthday felicitations and the emperor raises his cup, Music of Primal Unity should be played;

sentences.zh: 再舉酒，奏《文同之樂》。

translations.literal: when the cup is raised a second time, perform Music of Civil Unity."
translations.idiomatic: when the cup is raised again, Music of Civil Unity should be played."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 五年，始議重興二舞，詔曰：「正冬二節，朝會舊儀，廢於離亂之時，興自和平之代。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, deliberation began on reviving the Two Dances. An edict stated: "The court assemblies of the two mid-winter festivals are ancient rites; they were abandoned in times of turmoil and should be revived in an age of peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the court began discussing the revival of the Two Dances. An edict read: "The court assemblies held at the two mid-winter festivals are ancient rites; they were abandoned amid turmoil and should be restored in a time of peace.

sentences.zh: 將期備物，全系用心；

translations.literal: When the time comes to prepare the implements, everything depends on devoted effort;
translations.idiomatic: When the time comes to prepare the regalia, everything depends on wholehearted effort;

sentences.zh: 須議擇人，同為定制。

translations.literal: persons must be selected through deliberation and regulations established together.
translations.idiomatic: suitable persons must be chosen through deliberation so that standards may be set in common.

sentences.zh: 其正冬朝會禮節、樂章、二舞行列等事宜，差太常卿崔棁、御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允與太常寺官一一詳定。

translations.literal: As to the ritual procedures, hymns, formations of the Two Dances, and related matters for the mid-winter court assemblies — Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhi, Vice Censor-in-chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are dispatched to determine each in detail.
translations.idiomatic: For the ritual procedures, hymns, formations of the Two Dances, and related matters of the mid-winter court assemblies, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhi, Vice Censor-in-chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are assigned to work out each point in detail.

sentences.zh: 禮從新意，道在舊章，庶知治世之和，漸見移風之善。

translations.literal: Rites may follow new intentions, but the Way lies in old regulations — thus one may know the harmony of a well-governed age and gradually see the goodness of transforming customs."
translations.idiomatic: Rites may follow new intentions, yet the Way rests in ancient statutes — so that all may know the harmony of a well-governed age and gradually witness the good effect of transforming customs."

sentences.zh: 」其年秋，棁等具述制度上奏云：

translations.literal: That autumn, Zhi and the others fully set forth the regulations and memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, Zhi and his colleagues submitted a full account of the regulations, stating:

sentences.zh: 案《禮》云：「天子以德為車，以樂為禦。

translations.literal: According to the Rites: "The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his driver.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites states: "The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his driver.

sentences.zh: 」「大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。

translations.literal: ""Great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the seasons with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: ""Great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the seasons with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮；

translations.literal: ""It also says: "To secure superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual;
translations.idiomatic: ""It also says: "To secure superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual;

sentences.zh: 移風易俗，莫善於樂。

translations.literal: to transform customs and change habits, nothing is better than music.
translations.idiomatic: to transform customs and change habits, nothing is better than music.

sentences.zh: 」故樂書議舞云：夫樂在耳曰聲，在目曰容。

translations.literal: ""Therefore the Music Treatise, in discussing dance, says: What music presents to the ear is called sound; what it presents to the eye is called form.
translations.idiomatic: ""Thus the Music Treatise, in discussing dance, says: What music presents to the ear is sound; what it presents to the eye is form.

sentences.zh: 聲應乎耳，可以聽知；

translations.literal: Sound responds to the ear and can be known by hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Sound reaches the ear and can be known by hearing;

sentences.zh: 容藏於心，難以貌睹。

translations.literal: form is stored in the heart and is hard to see in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: form is stored in the heart and cannot easily be seen in one's bearing.

sentences.zh: 故聖人假幹戚羽旄以表其容，發揚蹈厲以見其意，聲容和合，則大樂備矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages borrowed shields, axes, feathers, and banners to display their form, and through vigorous stamping and leaping made their intent visible — when sound and form unite, great music is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages used shields, axes, feathers, and banners to display form, and through vigorous stamping and leaping revealed intent — when sound and form unite, great music is complete.

sentences.zh: 又案《義鏡》，問鼓吹十二案合於何所？

translations.literal: Again, according to the Mirror of Rites, the question was asked: To what do the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion music correspond?
translations.idiomatic: Again, according to the Mirror of Rites, it is asked: To what institution do the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion correspond?

sentences.zh: 答云：《周禮》鼓人掌六鼓四金，漢朝乃有黃門鼓吹。

translations.literal: The answer states: In the Rites of Zhou the Drum Master supervised six drums and four metal instruments; the Han dynasty then had the Yellow Gate wind-and-percussion.
translations.idiomatic: The answer states: In the Rites of Zhou the Drum Master supervised six drums and four metal instruments; under Han there was the Yellow Gate wind-and-percussion ensemble.

sentences.zh: 崔豹《古今註》云：因張騫使西域，得《摩訶兜勒》一曲，李延年增之，分為二十八曲。

translations.literal: Cui Bao's Notes Ancient and Modern states: Through Zhang Qian's mission to the Western Regions, the piece Mahadule was obtained; Li Yannian expanded it and divided it into twenty-eight pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bao's Notes Ancient and Modern states: When Zhang Qian was sent to the Western Regions, the piece Mahadule was obtained; Li Yannian expanded it and divided it into twenty-eight pieces.

sentences.zh: 梁置鼓吹清商令二人。

translations.literal: Liang established two Directors of Wind-and-Percussion and Pure Shang music.
translations.idiomatic: Liang appointed two Directors of Wind-and-Percussion and Pure Shang music.

sentences.zh: 唐又有堈鼓、金鉦、大鼓、長鳴、歌簫、笳、笛，合為鼓吹十二案，大享會則設於懸外。

translations.literal: Tang added the jar drum, golden chime, great drum, long call, singing pipe, horn, and flute — together forming the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion, which at great feasts were set up outside the suspended bells.
translations.idiomatic: Tang added the jar drum, golden chime, great drum, long call, singing pipe, horn, and flute — together forming the twelve wind-and-percussion sets, placed outside the suspended bells at great feasts.

sentences.zh: 此乃是設二舞及鼓吹十二案之由也。

translations.literal: This is the reason for establishing the Two Dances and the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion.
translations.idiomatic: This is the origin of establishing the Two Dances and the twelve wind-and-percussion sets.

sentences.zh: 今議一從令式，排列教習。

translations.literal: The present deliberation follows the statutes in full, arranging and training [the performers].
translations.idiomatic: The present plan follows the statutes entirely, arranging formations and training the performers.

sentences.zh: 文舞郎六十四人，分為八佾，每佾八人。

translations.literal: There are sixty-four civil dancers, divided into eight rows of eight dancers each.
translations.idiomatic: There are sixty-four civil dancers, divided into eight rows of eight each.

sentences.zh: 左手執籥。

translations.literal: In the left hand they hold the yue [reed pipe].
translations.idiomatic: They hold the yue reed pipe in the left hand.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云：「葦籥，伊耆氏之樂也。

translations.literal: The Rites states: "The reed yue is the music of the Yi'shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites states: "The reed yue is the music of the Yi'shi clan.

sentences.zh: 」《周禮》有「籥師教國子」，《爾雅》曰：籥如笛，三孔而短，大者七孔，謂之簅。

translations.literal: ""The Rites of Zhou has "the Yue Master teaches the sons of the state." The Erya says: The yue is like a flute, with three holes and short; the larger kind has seven holes and is called chan.
translations.idiomatic: ""The Rites of Zhou records "the Yue Master teaches the sons of the state." The Erya says: The yue resembles a flute, with three holes and short; the larger kind has seven holes and is called chan.

sentences.zh: 歷代已來，文舞所用，凡用籥六十有四。

translations.literal: Through successive dynasties, in civil dances sixty-four yue have been used in all.
translations.idiomatic: Down through the ages, civil dances have used sixty-four yue in all.

sentences.zh: 右手執翟，《周禮》所謂羽舞也。

translations.literal: In the right hand they hold the di [pheasant-feather staff]; the Rites of Zhou calls this the feather dance.
translations.idiomatic: They hold the di pheasant-feather staff in the right hand — what the Rites of Zhou calls the feather dance.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「舞幹羽於兩階。

translations.literal: The Documents states: "They danced shields and feathers on the two flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents states: "They danced with shields and feathers on the two flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 」翟，山雉也，以雉羽公析連攢而為之。

translations.literal: " The di is the mountain pheasant; it is made by taking pheasant feathers, splitting them evenly, and binding them together.
translations.idiomatic: " The di is the mountain pheasant; it is fashioned from pheasant feathers split evenly and bound together.

sentences.zh: 二人執纛前引，數於舞人之外。

translations.literal: Two men bearing great banners lead in front, stationed outside the dancers.
translations.idiomatic: Two men carrying great banners lead in front, positioned outside the ranks of dancers.

sentences.zh: 舞人冠進賢冠，服黃紗袍，白紗中單，皂領褾，白練衤蓋襠，白布大口袴，革帶，烏皮履，白布襪。

translations.literal: The dancers wear the Advance-the-Worthy cap, yellow gauze robes, white gauze under-garments, black collars and cuffs, white silk covering-bibs, white cloth baggy trousers, leather belts, black leather shoes, and white cloth socks.
translations.idiomatic: The dancers wear the Advance-the-Worthy cap, yellow gauze robes, white gauze under-shirts, black collars and cuffs, white silk covering-bibs, white cloth baggy trousers, leather belts, black leather shoes, and white cloth socks.

sentences.zh: 武舞郎六十四人，分為八佾。

translations.literal: There are sixty-four martial dancers, divided into eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: There are sixty-four martial dancers, divided into eight rows of eight.

sentences.zh: 左手執幹。

translations.literal: In the left hand they hold the gan [shield].
translations.idiomatic: They hold the shield in the left hand.

sentences.zh: 幹，楯也，今之旁牌，所以翳身也，其色赤，中畫獸形，故謂之朱幹。

translations.literal: The gan is a shield — today's side-board, used to cover the body; its color is red, with beast figures painted in the center, hence it is called the vermilion gan.
translations.idiomatic: The gan is a shield — what today would be called a side-board, used to screen the body; it is red, with beast figures painted at the center, hence the vermilion gan.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》所謂兵舞，取其武象，用楯六十有四。

translations.literal: What the Rites of Zhou calls the weapons dance takes its martial image and uses sixty-four shields.
translations.idiomatic: What the Rites of Zhou calls the weapons dance adopts a martial image and employs sixty-four shields in all.

sentences.zh: 右手執戚。

translations.literal: In the right hand they hold the qi [battle-axe].
translations.idiomatic: They hold the battle-axe in the right hand.

sentences.zh: 戚，斧也，上飾以玉，故謂之玉戚。

translations.literal: The qi is an axe, ornamented with jade above, hence it is called the jade qi.
translations.idiomatic: The qi is an axe ornamented with jade at the top, hence the jade qi.

sentences.zh: 二人執旌前引，旌似旗而小，絳色，畫升龍。

translations.literal: Two men bearing banners lead in front; banners resemble flags but are smaller, deep red in color, painted with ascending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Two men carrying banners lead in front; the banners resemble flags but are smaller, deep red, and painted with ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 二人執鼗鼓，二人執鐸。

translations.literal: Two men hold the tambourine-drums; two men hold the bells.
translations.idiomatic: Two men hold tambourine-drums; two men hold bells.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》有四金之奏，其三曰金鐸，以通鼓，形如大鈴，仰而振之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou has the performance of the four metals; the third is called the metal bell, used to set the drums in motion — shaped like a large hand-bell, struck by shaking it upward.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou describes the performance of the four metals; the third is the metal bell, used to signal the drums — shaped like a large hand-bell, shaken upward to sound it.

sentences.zh: 金錞二，每錞二人舉之，一人奏之。

translations.literal: There are two metal chun; for each chun two men raise it and one man plays it.
translations.idiomatic: There are two metal chun; for each one, two men lift it while one plays it.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》四金之奏，一曰金錞，以和鼓，銅鑄為之，其色黑，其形圓，若椎，上大下小，高三尺六寸有六分，圍二尺四寸，上有伏虎之狀，旁有耳，獸形銜镮。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou performance of the four metals, the first is called the metal chun, used to harmonize with the drums; cast in copper, its color is black, its shape round like a pestle, large above and small below, three feet six inches and six-tenths in height, two feet four inches in circumference, with a crouching tiger on top, ears at the sides, and beast-shaped rings.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou performance of the four metals, the first is the metal chun, used to harmonize with the drums; cast in copper, black in color, round like a pestle — large above and small below, three feet six inches and six-tenths high, two feet four inches around, topped with a crouching tiger, with ears at the sides and beast-shaped rings.

sentences.zh: 二人執鐃以次之。

translations.literal: Two men hold the nao and follow next in order.
translations.idiomatic: Two men hold the nao and follow in sequence.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》四金之奏，二曰金鐃，以止鼓，如鈴無舌，搖柄以鳴之。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou performance of the four metals, the second is called the metal nao, used to stop the drums — like a bell without a clapper, sounded by shaking the handle.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou performance of the four metals, the second is the metal nao, used to stop the drums — like a bell without a clapper, sounded by shaking its handle.

sentences.zh: 二人掌相在左，《禮》云：「治亂以相。

translations.literal: Two men supervise the xiang on the left; the Rites states: "To regulate order and disorder, use the xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Two men supervise the xiang on the left; the Rites states: "To regulate order and disorder, use the xiang.

sentences.zh: 」制如小鼓，用皮為表，實之以糠，撫之以節樂。

translations.literal: " Its form is like a small drum, with leather as the covering, filled with chaff, and stroked to mark the rhythm of the music.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaped like a small drum with a leather covering, filled with chaff, it is stroked to mark the musical beat.

sentences.zh: 二人掌雅在右，《禮》云：「訊疾以雅。

translations.literal: Two men supervise the ya on the right; the Rites states: "To examine swiftness, use the ya.
translations.idiomatic: Two men supervise the ya on the right; the Rites states: "To test for swiftness, use the ya.

sentences.zh: 」以木為之，狀如漆筒而弇口，大二尺圍，長五尺六寸，以羖皮鞔之，旁有二紐，髹畫，賓醉而出，以器築地，明行不失節。

translations.literal: " Made of wood, shaped like a lacquered tube with a narrowed mouth, two feet in circumference, five feet six inches long, covered with ram hide, with two toggles at the sides and lacquer decoration — when guests are drunk and depart, they strike the ground with the instrument so that their steps do not lose the beat.
translations.idiomatic: " Made of wood in the shape of a lacquered tube with a narrowed mouth, two feet around and five feet six inches long, covered with ram hide, with two toggles at the sides and lacquer decoration — when guests depart in drunkenness, they strike the ground with it so their steps keep proper rhythm.

sentences.zh: 武舞人服弁，平巾幘，金支緋絲大袖，緋絲布裲襠，甲金飾，白練𧞔襠，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口布袴，烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Martial dancers wear caps, plain headcloths, gold-embroidered scarlet silk large sleeves, scarlet silk cloth vests, gold-decorated armor, white silk covering-bibs, brocade belts with rising serpents, leopard-pattern baggy cloth trousers, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Martial dancers wear caps, plain headcloths, gold-embroidered scarlet silk large sleeves, scarlet silk vests, gold-trimmed armor, white silk covering-bibs, brocade belts with serpent motifs, leopard-pattern baggy trousers, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 工人二十，數於舞人之外。

translations.literal: Twenty artisans are stationed outside the dancers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty artisans are positioned outside the ranks of dancers.

sentences.zh: 武弁朱翙，革帶，烏皮履，白練礻蓋襠，白布襪。

translations.literal: [They wear] martial caps with vermilion pheasant feathers, leather belts, black leather shoes, white silk covering-bibs, and white cloth socks.
translations.idiomatic: They wear martial caps with vermilion pheasant plumes, leather belts, black leather shoes, white silk covering-bibs, and white cloth socks.

sentences.zh: 殿庭仍加鼓吹十二案。

translations.literal: The palace courtyard also adds the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion.
translations.idiomatic: The palace courtyard will also add the twelve wind-and-percussion sets.

sentences.zh: 《義鏡》云：常設氈案，以氈為床也。

translations.literal: The Mirror of Rites states: Felt platforms are regularly set up, using felt as a bedding.
translations.idiomatic: The Mirror of Rites states: Felt platforms were regularly set up, using felt as bedding.

sentences.zh: 今請制大床十二，慶容九人，振作歌樂，其床為熊羆貙豹騰倚之狀以承之，象百獸率舞之意。

translations.literal: It is now requested to fashion twelve large platforms, with nine persons of celebratory countenance raising up song and music; the platforms are made in the shapes of bears, panthers, leopards, and similar beasts leaping and leaning to support them, symbolizing the meaning of the hundred beasts leading the dance.
translations.idiomatic: We now propose twelve large platforms, each with nine performers of festive mien raising song and music; the platforms are shaped as bears, panthers, leopards, and like beasts leaping and straining to support them, expressing the idea of the hundred beasts leading the dance.

sentences.zh: 分置於建鼓之外，各三案，每案羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌二人，簫二人，笳二人。

translations.literal: Placed separately outside the established drums, three platforms at each [side], each platform with one feathered-banner drum, one great drum, one metal chun, two singers, two flute players, and two horn players.
translations.idiomatic: They are set apart outside the established drums, three platforms on each side; each platform has one feathered-banner drum, one great drum, one metal chun, two singers, two flute players, and two horn players.

sentences.zh: 十二案，樂工百有八人，舞郎一百三十有二人，取年十五已上，弱冠已下，容止端正者。

translations.literal: For the twelve platforms, there are one hundred eight musicians and one hundred thirty-two dancers, selected from those fifteen years of age and above, before the capped years, of upright bearing and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: For the twelve platforms there are 108 musicians and 132 dancers, drawn from those aged fifteen or above but not yet capped, of upright bearing and deportment.

sentences.zh: 其歌曲名號、樂章詞句，中書條奏，差官修撰。

translations.literal: As to the song titles, hymn names, and lyrical texts — the Secretariat is to submit them in detailed memorial and dispatch officials to compose them.
translations.idiomatic: The song titles, hymn names, and lyrical texts are to be submitted in a detailed memorial by the Secretariat, and officials dispatched to compose them.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The memorial] was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史·崔棁傳》：高祖詔太常復文武二舞，詳定正冬朝會禮及樂章。

translations.literal: (From the Ouyang History, Biography of Cui Zhi: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and martial Two Dances and to determine in detail the ritual and hymns for the mid-winter court assembly.
translations.idiomatic: (From Ouyang Xiu's History, Biography of Cui Zhi: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and martial Two Dances and work out in detail the mid-winter court assembly rites and hymns.

sentences.zh: 自唐末之亂，禮樂制度亡失已久，棁與御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允等草定之。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhi together with Vice Censor-in-chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhi, together with Vice Censor-in-chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted the regulations.

sentences.zh: 其年冬至，高祖會朝崇元殿，廷設宮懸，二舞在北，登歌在上。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice, Gaozu held court at the Hall of Venerated Origins; the courtyard was set with suspended palace music, the Two Dances to the north, ascending song above.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice, Gaozu held court in the Hall of Venerated Origins; suspended palace music was set up in the court, the Two Dances to the north and the ascending song above.

sentences.zh: 文舞郎八佾六十有四人，冠進賢。

translations.literal: The civil dancers numbered eight rows, sixty-four in all, wearing the Advance-the-Worthy cap.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixty-four civil dancers in eight rows, wearing the Advance-the-Worthy cap.

sentences.zh: 黃紗袍，白中單，白練礻蓋襠，白布大口袴，革帶履，左執枿，右秉翟，執纛引者二人。

translations.literal: Yellow gauze robes, white under-garments, white silk covering-bibs, white cloth baggy trousers, leather belts and shoes — in the left hand the yue, in the right the di, with two men bearing great banners leading.
translations.idiomatic: They wore yellow gauze robes, white under-shirts, white silk covering-bibs, white cloth baggy trousers, leather belts and shoes — yue in the left hand, di in the right, with two banner-bearers leading.

sentences.zh: 武舞郎八佾六十有四人，服平巾幘，緋絲布大袖繡襠，甲金飾，白練礻蓋襠，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口袴，烏靴，左執幹，右執戚，執旌引者二人。

translations.literal: The martial dancers numbered eight rows, sixty-four in all, wearing plain headcloths, scarlet silk cloth large sleeves with embroidered vests, gold-decorated armor, white silk covering-bibs, brocade belts with rising serpents, leopard-pattern baggy trousers, and black boots — in the left hand the gan, in the right the qi, with two men bearing banners leading.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixty-four martial dancers in eight rows, wearing plain headcloths, scarlet silk large sleeves with embroidered vests, gold-trimmed armor, white silk covering-bibs, brocade serpent belts, leopard-pattern baggy trousers, and black boots — shield in the left hand, battle-axe in the right, with two banner-bearers leading.

sentences.zh: 加鼓吹十二案，負以熊豹，以象百獸率舞。

translations.literal: The twelve wind-and-percussion platforms were added, borne on [figures of] bears and leopards to symbolize the hundred beasts leading the dance.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve wind-and-percussion platforms were added, borne on bear and leopard figures to symbolize the hundred beasts leading the dance.

sentences.zh: 案設羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌簫、笳各二人。

translations.literal: Each platform was set with one feathered-banner drum, one great drum, one metal chun, and two each of singers, flutes, and horns.
translations.idiomatic: Each platform had one feathered-banner drum, one great drum, one metal chun, and two singers, two flutes, and two horns apiece.

sentences.zh: 王公上壽，天子舉爵，奏《元同》；

translations.literal: When the princes and dukes offered longevity wishes and the Son of Heaven raised his goblet, Music of Primal Unity was performed;
translations.idiomatic: When the princes and dukes offered birthday felicitations and the emperor raised his goblet, Music of Primal Unity was played;

sentences.zh: 二舉，登歌奏《文同》；

translations.literal: at the second raising, the ascending song performed Music of Civil Unity;
translations.idiomatic: at the second raising, the ascending song was Music of Civil Unity;

sentences.zh: 舉食，文舞《昭德》，武舞《成功》之曲。

translations.literal: when food was raised, the civil dance performed Manifest Virtue and the martial dance Accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: at the serving of food, the civil dance Manifest Virtue and the martial dance Accomplishment were performed.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，高祖大悅，賜棁金帛，群臣左右睹者皆贊嘆之。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silks on Zhi; all the officials near and far who witnessed it praised and exclaimed over it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites concluded, Gaozu was greatly pleased and rewarded Zhi with gold and silks; all officials who witnessed it, near and far, praised and marveled.

sentences.zh: 然禮樂廢久，而制作簡繆，又繼以龜茲部《霓裳法曲》，參亂雅音。

translations.literal: Yet ritual and music had been abandoned long, and the compositions were crude and erroneous; moreover the Kucha Directorate's Rainbow Skirt Dharma Melody was subsequently mixed in, disturbing the elegant tones.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual and music had long lain in ruin, and what was composed was crude and faulty; moreover the Kucha directorate's Rainbow Skirt Dharma Melody was mixed in, corrupting the refined tones.

sentences.zh: 其樂工舞郎，多教坊伶人、百工商賈、州縣避役之人，又無老師良工教習。

translations.literal: Most of the musicians and dancers were entertainers from the Directorate of Entertainments, craftsmen and merchants, and persons from prefectures and counties avoiding corvée labor — and there were no veteran masters or skilled artisans to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the musicians and dancers were Directorate of Entertainments performers, craftsmen and merchants, and men from the prefectures and counties dodging corvée — and there were no veteran masters or skilled teachers to train them.

sentences.zh: 明年正旦，復奏於庭，而登歌發聲，悲離煩慝，如《薤露》、《虞殯》之音，舞者行列進退，皆不應節，聞者皆悲憤。

translations.literal: The next year at New Year's Day it was performed again in the court, but the ascending song sounded mournful, troubled, and vexed — like the tones of Thoroughwort Dew and Yu's Funeral — and the dancers' formations advancing and retreating did not match the beat; all who heard were grieved and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: The following New Year's Day it was performed again in court, but the ascending song sounded mournful, troubled, and strained — like Thoroughwort Dew or Yu's Funeral — and the dancers' formations advancing and retreating fell out of rhythm; all who heard it were grieved and indignant.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，太常少卿陶穀奏廢二舞。）〉

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the Two Dances.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the Two Dances.)〉

sentences.zh: 漢高祖受命之年，秋九月，權太常卿張昭上疏，奏改一代樂名，其略曰？

translations.literal: In the year Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial proposing to change the music names of the dynasty — in summary states:
translations.idiomatic: In the year Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial proposing to rename the dynasty's musical works — in summary states:

sentences.zh: 昔周公相成王，制禮作樂，殿庭遍奏六代舞，所謂《雲門》、《大咸》、《大韶》、《大夏》、《大》、《大武》也。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, he instituted ritual and composed music; in the hall all six dynastic dances were performed in turn — namely Cloud Gate, Great Xian, Great Shao, Great Xia, Great Huo, and Great Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, he established ritual and composed music; the hall performed all six dynastic dances in turn — Cloud Gate, Great Xian, Great Shao, Great Xia, Great Huo, and Great Wu.

sentences.zh: 周室既衰，王綱不振，諸樂多廢，惟《大韶》、《大武》二曲存焉。

translations.literal: When the Zhou house declined, the royal ordinances were not upheld, and most of the music was abandoned; only the Great Shao and Great Wu two pieces remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou house declined and royal authority faltered, most of the music was abandoned; only Great Shao and Great Wu survived.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，名為二舞：文舞，《韶》也；

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward they were called the Two Dances: the civil dance was the Shao;
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward they were known as the Two Dances: the civil dance was the Shao;

sentences.zh: 武舞，《武》也。

translations.literal: the martial dance was the Wu.
translations.idiomatic: the martial dance was the Wu.

sentences.zh: 漢時改為《文始》、《五行之舞》，歷代因而不改。

translations.literal: In Han times they were changed to the Dance of Literary Inception and the Dance of the Five Phases; successive dynasties followed without alteration.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han they were renamed the Dance of Literary Inception and the Dance of the Five Phases; successive dynasties followed without change.

sentences.zh: 貞觀作樂之時，祖孝孫改隋文舞為《治康之舞》武舞為《凱安之舞》。

translations.literal: When music was composed in the Zhenguan era, Zu Xiaosun changed the Sui civil dance to the Dance of Governing Tranquility and the martial dance to the Dance of Triumphant Peace.
translations.idiomatic: When music was composed in the Zhenguan era, Zu Xiaosun changed the Sui civil dance to the Dance of Governing Tranquility and the martial dance to the Dance of Triumphant Peace.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，有《秦王破陣樂》、《功成慶善樂》二舞，樂府又用為二舞，是舞有四焉。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan period there were also the Prince of Qin Breaks the Battle Array and the Music of Accomplished Merit and Celebrating Goodness — two dances that the Music Bureau also used as two dances, so that there were four dances in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan period there were also Prince of Qin Breaks the Battle Array and Music of Accomplished Merit and Celebrating Goodness — two dances that the Music Bureau likewise adopted, so that there were four dances in all.

sentences.zh: 前朝行用年深，不可遽廢，俟國家偃伯靈臺，即別召工師，更其節奏，今改其名，具書如左：祖孝孫所定二舞名，文舞曰《治康之舞》，請改《治安之舞》；

translations.literal: The former dynasty had used them for many years and they cannot be abruptly abolished; when the state rests its weapons and the Spirit Terrace is at peace, skilled artisans will be summoned separately to revise their rhythms — for now their names are changed, recorded in full below: the two dances fixed by Zu Xiaosun — the civil dance called the Dance of Governing Tranquility, requested to be changed to the Dance of Securing Tranquility;
translations.idiomatic: The former dynasty had used them for many years and they cannot be abruptly abolished; when the state lays down its weapons and the Spirit Terrace is at peace, skilled artisans will be summoned to revise their rhythms — for now their names are changed, as recorded below: the two dances fixed by Zu Xiaosun — the civil dance called the Dance of Governing Tranquility, proposed to be renamed the Dance of Securing Tranquility;

sentences.zh: 武舞曰《凱安之舞》，請改為《振德之舞》。

translations.literal: the martial dance called the Dance of Triumphant Peace, requested to be changed to the Dance of Shaking Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: the martial dance called the Dance of Triumphant Peace, proposed to be renamed the Dance of Shaking Virtue.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中二舞名，文舞《功成慶善樂》，前朝名《九功舞》，請改為《觀象之舞》；

translations.literal: The two dances of the Zhenguan period — the civil dance Music of Accomplished Merit and Celebrating Goodness, formerly called the Dance of the Nine Merits under the previous dynasty, requested to be changed to the Dance of Contemplating Images;
translations.idiomatic: The two Zhenguan dances — the civil dance Music of Accomplished Merit and Celebrating Goodness, formerly the Dance of the Nine Merits under the previous dynasty, proposed to be renamed the Dance of Contemplating Images;

sentences.zh: 武舞《秦王破陣樂》，前朝名為《七德舞》，請改為《講功之舞》。

translations.literal: the martial dance Prince of Qin Breaks the Battle Array, formerly called the Dance of the Seven Virtues under the previous dynasty, requested to be changed to the Dance of Expounding Merit.
translations.idiomatic: the martial dance Prince of Qin Breaks the Battle Array, formerly the Dance of the Seven Virtues, proposed to be renamed the Dance of Expounding Merit.

sentences.zh: 其《治安》、《振德》二舞，請依舊郊廟行用，以文舞降神，武舞送神。

translations.literal: As to the two dances Securing Tranquility and Shaking Virtue, they are requested to continue in use at suburban and temple rites as before — the civil dance to welcome the spirit, the martial dance to send off the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The two dances Securing Tranquility and Shaking Virtue are proposed to continue in use at suburban and temple rites as before — the civil dance to welcome the spirit, the martial dance to send it off.

sentences.zh: 其《觀象》、《講功》二舞，請依舊宴會行用。

translations.literal: As to the two dances Contemplating Images and Expounding Merit, they are requested to continue in use at banquets as before.
translations.idiomatic: The two dances Contemplating Images and Expounding Merit are proposed to continue in use at banquets as before.

sentences.zh: 又請改《十二和樂》云：

translations.literal: He also requested to change the Twelve Harmony Music, stating:
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed changing the Twelve Harmony Music, stating:

sentences.zh: 昔周朝奏六代之樂，即今二舞之類是也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Zhou court performed the music of the six dynasties — the same category as today's Two Dances.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Zhou court performed the music of the six dynasties — the same category as today's Two Dances.

sentences.zh: 其賓祭常用，別有《九夏之樂》，即《肆夏》、《皇夏》等是也，梁武帝善音樂，改《九夏》為《十二雅》，前朝祖孝孫改雅為和，示不相沿也。

translations.literal: For guest rites and sacrifices in common use there was separately the Music of the Nine Summers — namely Manifest Summer, Imperial Summer, and the like; Emperor Wu of Liang was skilled in music and changed the Nine Summers to the Twelve Elegances; under the previous dynasty Zu Xiaosun changed elegance to harmony, showing that one does not simply follow precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For guest rites and sacrifices there was separately the Music of the Nine Summers — Manifest Summer, Imperial Summer, and the like; Emperor Wu of Liang, skilled in music, changed the Nine Summers to the Twelve Elegances; under the previous dynasty Zu Xiaosun changed elegance to harmony, to show that one does not simply follow precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣今改和為成，取《韶》樂九成之義也。

translations.literal: Your subject now changes harmony to accomplishment, taking the meaning of the Shao music's nine-tenths accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: I now propose changing harmony to accomplishment, taking the meaning of the Shao music's nine-tenths accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 《十二成樂曲》名：祭天神奏《豫和之樂》，請改為《禋成》；

translations.literal: Names of the Twelve Accomplishment pieces: for sacrifices to Heaven, Music of Harmonious Expectation is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of the Sacrificial Rite;
translations.idiomatic: Names of the Twelve Accomplishment pieces: for sacrifices to Heaven, Harmonious Expectation is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of the Sacrificial Rite;

sentences.zh: 祭地祇奏《順和》，請改為《順成》；

translations.literal: for sacrifices to Earth, Music of Compliant Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Compliant Accomplishment;
translations.idiomatic: for sacrifices to Earth, Compliant Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Compliant Accomplishment;

sentences.zh: 祭宗廟奏《永和》，請改為《裕成》；

translations.literal: for sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Music of Eternal Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Abundant Accomplishment;
translations.idiomatic: for sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Eternal Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Abundant Accomplishment;

sentences.zh: 祭天地、宗廟，登歌奏《肅和》，請改為《肅成》；

translations.literal: for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the ascending song performs Music of Solemn Harmony — requested to be changed to Solemn Accomplishment;
translations.idiomatic: for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the ascending song is Solemn Harmony — proposed to be renamed Solemn Accomplishment;

sentences.zh: 皇帝臨軒奏《太和》，請改為《政成》；

translations.literal: when the emperor presides at court, Music of Grand Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of Governance;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor presides at court, Grand Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of Governance;

sentences.zh: 王公出入奏《舒和》，請改為《弼成》；

translations.literal: when princes and dukes enter and depart, Music of Easy Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of Assistance;
translations.idiomatic: when princes and dukes enter and depart, Easy Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of Assistance;

sentences.zh: 皇帝食舉及飲宴奏《休和》，請改為《德成》；

translations.literal: when the emperor raises his cup at meals and drinking banquets, Music of Restful Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of Virtue;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor raises his cup at meals and banquets, Restful Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of Virtue;

sentences.zh: 皇帝受朝、皇后入宮奏《正和》，請改為《骍成》；

translations.literal: when the emperor receives court and the empress enters the palace, Music of Correct Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of the Crimson;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor receives court and the empress enters the palace, Correct Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of the Crimson;

sentences.zh: 皇太子軒懸出入奏《承和》，請改為《允成》；

translations.literal: when the heir apparent's suspended bells enter and depart, Music of Assumed Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of Assent;
translations.idiomatic: when the heir apparent's suspended bells enter and depart, Assumed Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of Assent;

sentences.zh: 元日、冬至皇帝禮會，登歌奏《昭和》，請改為《慶成》；

translations.literal: at New Year's Day and the winter solstice when the emperor holds ceremonial assembly, the ascending song performs Music of Bright Harmony — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of Celebration;
translations.idiomatic: at New Year's Day and the winter solstice court assembly, the ascending song is Bright Harmony — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of Celebration;

sentences.zh: 郊廟俎入奏《雍和》，請改為《骍成》；

translations.literal: when the offering stand enters at suburban and temple rites, Music of Harmonious Abundance is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of the Crimson;
translations.idiomatic: when the offering stand enters at suburban and temple rites, Harmonious Abundance is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of the Crimson;

sentences.zh: 皇帝祭享、酌獻、讀祝文及飲福、受胙奏《壽和》，請改為《壽成》。

translations.literal: when the emperor sacrifices, offers libations, reads the prayer text, drinks the blessed wine, and receives the sacrificial meat, Music of Longevity Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Accomplishment of Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor sacrifices, offers libations, reads the prayer, drinks the blessed wine, and receives the sacrificial meat, Longevity Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Accomplishment of Longevity.

sentences.zh: 祖孝孫元定《十二和曲》，開元朝又奏三和，遂有《十五和》之名。

translations.literal: Zu Xiaosun originally fixed the Twelve Harmony pieces; in the Kaiyuan reign three more harmonies were added, and thus the name Fifteen Harmonies arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaosun originally fixed the Twelve Harmony pieces; in the Kaiyuan reign three more were added, giving rise to the name Fifteen Harmonies.

sentences.zh: 凡制作禮法，動依典故，梁置《十二雅》，蓋取十二天之成數，契八音十二律之變，輒益三和，有乖稽古。

translations.literal: In composing ritual and law, one should always follow ancient precedent; Liang established the Twelve Elegances, taking the accomplished number of the twelve heavens and matching the transformations of the eight tones and twelve pitches — to add three harmonies at will violates investigation of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In composing ritual and law one should always follow ancient precedent; Liang established the Twelve Elegances, taking the accomplished number of the twelve heavens and matching the eight tones and twelve pitches — to add three harmonies at will violates investigation of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 又緣祠祭所用，不可盡去，臣取其一焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, because those used in sacrificial rites cannot all be removed, your subject takes one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because some pieces used in sacrificial rites cannot all be removed, I retain one of them.

sentences.zh: 祭孔宣父、齊太公廟降神奏《宣和》，請改為《師雅之樂》；

translations.literal: For sacrifices at the temples of Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi to welcome the spirit, Music of Manifest Harmony is performed — requested to be changed to Music of Masters' Elegance;
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices at the temples of Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi to welcome the spirit, Manifest Harmony is played — proposed to be renamed Music of Masters' Elegance;

sentences.zh: 三公升殿、會訖下階履行奏《祴和》，請廢，同用《弼成》；

translations.literal: when the Three Dukes ascend the hall and, when the assembly ends, descend the steps and process, Music of Blessing Harmony is performed — requested to be abolished and the same piece as Assistance used instead;
translations.idiomatic: when the Three Dukes ascend the hall and, when the assembly ends, descend and process, Blessing Harmony is played — proposed to be abolished and Assistance used instead;

sentences.zh: 享先農、耕籍田奏《豐和》，請廢，同用《順成》。

translations.literal: for offerings to the Spirit of Agriculture and plowing the sacred field, Music of Abundant Harmony is performed — requested to be abolished and the same piece as Compliant Accomplishment used.
translations.idiomatic: for offerings to the Spirit of Agriculture and plowing the sacred field, Abundant Harmony is played — proposed to be abolished and Compliant Accomplishment used instead.

sentences.zh: 已上四舞、《十二成》、《雅樂》等曲，今具錄合用處所及樂章首數，一一條例在下。

translations.literal: The four dances, Twelve Accomplishments, elegant music, and other pieces listed above are now fully recorded with their places of use and the number of hymn stanzas, each itemized below.
translations.idiomatic: The four dances, Twelve Accomplishments, elegant music, and other pieces listed above are now fully recorded with their places of use and the number of hymn stanzas, each itemized below.

sentences.zh: 其歌詞文不錄。

translations.literal: The texts of the lyrics are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The lyric texts are not recorded here.
